items.q: It’s gotten way out of hand, because you can buy, say, a Charlie Parker album – CD today, LP formerly – and you might have one side of nothing but 30 different stabs at Salt Peanuts, some of which last 4 seconds.

items.title: George Avakian interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 21, 1998
items.q: Gillespie and Parker have a quintet at Billy Berg’s and we’ll go tomorrow night if you’re free.” I said fine. That was my first exposure to live bebop.

ctx.x: Oh that was a kind of an interesting thing because I was already aware of what was beginning to happen before the war. You see I got drafted straight off the campus, I was inducted about two or three months after I graduated from Yale. The first inkling was in the form of Dizzy Gillespie’s playing. And I first heard Dizzy in I guess it was 1938 because I remember discussing it with Marshall Stearns. His records came out and there were solos of Dizzy’s on various releases, including of course the Cab Calloway…

And that’s when he married my sister and moved out to Los Angeles, his home.
